kindHint.ACCESS: A copy of everything we hold about the person, as one package (GDPR arts. 15 and 20).
kindHint.ERASURE: The person's details erased or anonymised; what the law keeps stays, with why (GDPR art. 17).
kindHint.CORRECTION: Wrong details corrected in the person's own record (GDPR art. 16).

held.CLOSED: The request is closed: it changes no more.
held.NOT_STARTED: Check the person's identity first: the work on a request starts with it (GDPR art. 12(6)).
held.IDENTITY_NOT_CHECKED: The person's identity is not checked yet (GDPR art. 12(6)): check it before the request is done.
held.IDENTITY_CHECKED: The identity was checked already: the check is recorded once.
held.EXTENDED: The request was extended once already: an extension never changes (GDPR art. 12(3)).
held.TOO_LATE_TO_EXTEND: An extension is decided and told within the first month (GDPR art. 12(3)): that month has passed.
held.NOT_ACCESS: Only an access request has a data package.
held.NOT_ERASURE: Only an erasure request erases or anonymises the person.
held.NO_PACKAGE: Collect the person's data package first: an access request is done once it is handed over.
held.PACKAGE_DELETED: The data package was deleted on its date (30 days after it was made): collect it again while the request is open.
held.NOT_ERASED: Anonymise the person first (what the law keeps stays, with why): an erasure request is done once that is recorded.
held.ERASED: The person was anonymised on this request already: what was erased and kept is recorded.

requests.name: Data requests answered within 30 days
requests.late_one: 1 request is late: answer it now.
requests.late_other: {count} requests are late: answer them now.
requests.law: GDPR art. 12(3): within one month of receipt, extended once by up to two months.

retention.name: Retention rules set
retention.none: No retention rule yet: nothing says how long personal data is kept.
retention.reporting_one: 1 rule, only reporting: nothing is deleted until a person switches it on.
retention.reporting_other: {count} rules, all only reporting: nothing is deleted until a person switches one on.
retention.law: GDPR art. 5(1)(e): kept no longer than needed; c.c. art. 2220: accounts 10 years.

req.title: Data requests
req.intro: Access, erasure and correction requests of a person, each with its 30-day clock (GDPR arts. 12, 15–17, 20).
req.lateBanner_one: 1 request passed its due day: the law asks for an answer within the month.
req.lateBanner_other: {count} requests passed their due day: the law asks for an answer within the month.

empty.kind: No request of this kind here.
empty.hint: A person asks by mail, letter or phone: record it with New data request; the 30-day clock starts when it came in.

held.manage: You may read data requests but not act on them.
held.erase: Only a person with the right to erase personal data may anonymise someone.

record.title: {kind} request · {person}
record.subtitle: {company} · {kind}
record.clockLaw: GDPR art. 12(3): answered within one month of receipt; extended once, within that month, by up to two months with the reason told to the person.
record.identityNot: Not checked yet: the work on the request starts with it (GDPR art. 12(6)).
record.eraseIntro: See what is erased and what the law keeps before anything changes; you type the person's name to confirm.
record.erased: Done: {anonymised} anonymised, {deleted} deleted, {kept} kept with why.
record.correctionIntro: Correct the details in the person's own record, then mark the request done.

pkg.title: Data package
pkg.intro: One ZIP of everything we hold about the person: data.json, a file per kind of record, their files, a README and the checksums (GDPR arts. 15, 20).
pkg.collectingNote: You can close this window: the package is made in the background and appears here when ready.
pkg.failed: The package could not be made. Collect it again; if it fails again, tell the administrator.

form.how: Say how the identity was checked (3 characters or more).

identity.title: Identity checked
identity.intro: Record how you checked that the request comes from the person: the work on it starts now.
identity.label: How was it checked?
identity.hint: For example: the reply came from the e-mail on record. Never a document number.

extend.title: Extend the request
extend.intro: Once, within the first month, by one or two more months when the request is complex or there are many (GDPR art. 12(3)). Tell the person why.
extend.label: Why it is extended
extend.hint: What makes the request complex, as told to the person.

refuse.title: Refuse the request
refuse.intro: Only when it is manifestly unfounded or excessive (GDPR art. 12(5)); the person may complain to the Garante.
refuse.label: Why it is refused

withdraw.title: The person withdrew it
withdraw.intro: The person no longer wants the request: it closes.
withdraw.label: Note

done.identity: Identity check recorded: the work on the request starts.
done.extended: Extended: the new due day is set.
done.collecting: Collecting the package: it appears here when ready.
done.erased: The person is anonymised; what the law keeps stays, with why.

new.title: New data request
new.intro: Record a request a person made by mail, letter or phone. The 30-day clock starts when it came in.

findHint.CONTACT: Part of the customer's code or name.
findHint.PROSPECT: Part of the inquiry's number, the prospect's company or e-mail.
findHint.REPORTER: Part of the report's number or the product.
findHint.USER: Part of the name or e-mail.
findHint.WORKER: Part of the name or the employee code.

new.noneFound: Nobody found: try another part of the name or number.
new.reporterHint: The list shows the report's number only: the reporter's name is shown once the request is recorded.
new.noLookup: You cannot look up a {what} here: it needs the right “{right}”. Ask someone who has it to record the request.
new.receivedHint: When the request came in: the 30-day clock starts here.
new.noteHint: What they asked and how (a mail, a letter). Never a document number or a health detail.

held.person: Find and pick the person first.
held.otherCompany: This person belongs to another company: record the request in that company.
held.received: Say when the request came in.
held.future: A request is recorded when it came in: now or before.
held.note: The note is at most 2000 characters.

erase.title: Anonymise {name}?
erase.intro: What is erased, what stays because the law requires it, and the decision is logged with your reason (GDPR art. 17).

blocked.PORTAL_USER: This person still signs in to the portal with the contact's e-mail: end their portal access first (Portal access › End access), then anonymise.
blocked.STILL_ACTIVE: This person still works here (an active employee or floor account): anonymise them after they left.
blocked.ACCOUNT_OPEN: This office account is still open: deactivate it first (Admin › Users), then anonymise.
blocked.NOT_A_PROSPECT: This inquiry names a contact of a customer, not a prospect: anonymise the contact instead.
blocked.TOO_MANY: This person has more records than one erasure writes at once: ask the administrator to split it.
blocked.MAIL_SENDING: A mail to this person is being sent right now: try again in two minutes, once it has gone.

anonymised.title: Anonymised
anonymised.intro: The person's details are blanked or replaced; the rest of the record (the business data) stays.
anonymised.note: The person's details go; the record stays.

kept.title: Kept because the law requires it
kept.intro: These stay as they are, each with the law's reason; invoices keep the business data.

why.FISCAL: Fiscal and accounting records are kept 10 years (c.c. art. 2220; DPR 633/72 art. 39; GDPR art. 17(3)(b)).
why.DISPUTE: Kept while a dispute is open (a complaint, a return, a service case or a labour dispute): needed to settle it (GDPR art. 17(3)(e)).
why.SAFETY_REPORT: Kept while the product-safety report is being assessed: the maker may need to reach the reporter (Reg. (EU) 2023/988; GDPR art. 17(3)(b)).
why.EMPLOYMENT: Employment records are kept 5 years after the employment ends (D.L. 112/2008 art. 39; GDPR art. 17(3)(b)).
why.HEALTH: Health surveillance and accident records are kept 10 years after the employment ends (D.Lgs. 81/2008 art. 25; GDPR art. 17(3)(b)).
why.CUSTOMER: The customer record names the person and the orders and invoices refer to it (c.c. art. 2220: 10 years; GDPR art. 17(3)(b)).
why.MEASUREMENTS: The measurements a garment was made to, for the legal guarantee (D.Lgs. 206/2005 art. 132: 26 months); their photos go on their own date.
why.ALREADY_ERASED: Already anonymised earlier: nothing of the person is left in it.
why.NOTICE_PROOF: The proof the person was given the privacy notice (GDPR arts. 5(2), 13): it names the notice's version, not the person's data.
why.LEGAL_HOLD: The file is on legal hold (a dispute, an inspection or a claim needs it as it is; GDPR art. 17(3)(e)).
why.RETAINED: Kept until its retention date: the law or a contract keeps the file until then (GDPR art. 17(3)(b)).

type.StoredFile: Files attached to what they sent

erase.historyScope: History: the changes to the person's own records are blanked; a mention of them in another record's history is not searched (each erasure record says what was blanked).

held.nothing: Nothing of this person is left to erase.
held.reason: Say why the person is anonymised (3 characters or more).
held.reasonLong: The reason is at most 1000 characters.
held.typed: Type the person's name exactly as shown.

erase.reasonHint: What they asked and how (a mail, a letter), without their details: it goes into the history.
erase.code: Anonymise asks for a fresh code from your authenticator, every time.
erase.logged: The decision is logged with your reason; the history never holds the person's name.

stepUp.title: Confirm it's you
stepUp.erase: Anonymising a person asks for a fresh code every time.
stepUp.apply: Switching a rule on to apply asks for a fresh code: from then on the sweep changes records for real.
stepUp.shorten: A shorter period (or another action while the rule applies) asks for a fresh code.

problem.conflict: Someone changed this meanwhile: it was read again. Look and try again.
problem.failed: That did not work. Try again.
problem.forbidden: Your role does not allow this here.
problem.invalid: It was refused as it is: check the fields.
problem.notFound: It is not there any more.
problem.rateLimited: Too many tries: wait a moment.
problem.stepUpClosed: Nothing changed: the code was not given.
problem.unavailable: The factory system did not answer. Try again.

ret.title: Retention rules
ret.intro: Per record type: how long it is kept, then delete, anonymise or archive, with the legal reason (GDPR art. 5(1)(e)).

gate.title: Nothing is deleted by itself
gate.body: A rule only reports what it would do until a person switches it on to apply, with a fresh code (GATE-PRIVACY). Every period is UNVERIFIED until the privacy consultant sets it.
gate.schedule: The sweep runs every night at 02:50 (Rome time).

ret.failed: The retention rules did not load.
ret.emptyHint: Add one per record type: how long, then what, and why the law asks for it.
ret.unverifiedLong: UNVERIFIED: a made-up period until the privacy consultant sets it (GATE-PRIVACY). The rule only reports until a person switches it on.

held.manage: You may read the rules but not change them.
held.SWITCHED_OFF: The rule is switched off: switch it on again first.
held.APPLYING: The sweep already applies this rule.
held.NOT_APPLYING: The sweep only reports this rule.
held.UNKNOWN_TYPE: The sweep knows nothing of this record type: the rule can only report.
held.NO_ACTION: No sweep may delete, anonymise or archive this record type: the rule can only report.

NEVER_DELETED.long: The database never deletes this record (an export expires, its file goes): the rule can only report it.

ARCHIVE_STAYS.long: Archived where it is: nothing is erased (the fiscal archive keeps the document and its file for the law).

NOT_YET.long: Not yet: the database keeps it a little longer (a closed error item 30 days, a job run 7 days).

failure.UNKNOWN_TYPE: The sweep knows nothing of this record type.
failure.DB_REFUSED: The database refused: nothing was applied; tried again at the next sweep.
failure.STOPPED: It stopped before the end: nothing was applied.

ReportRun.name: Report runs
ReportRun.countsFrom: From when the report was run.

does.DELETE: Deletes the run (who ran which report, with which filters); the reports themselves stay.
does.ANONYMISE: A report run cannot be anonymised: the rule only reports.
does.ARCHIVE: A report run cannot be archived: the rule only reports.

CronRun.name: Scheduled job runs
CronRun.countsFrom: From when the run finished (a running one is never due).

does.DELETE: Deletes the finished run (job, time, result, error); never one still running, never within 7 days of its end.
does.ANONYMISE: A job run cannot be anonymised: the rule only reports.
does.ARCHIVE: A job run cannot be archived: the rule only reports.

IntegrationErrorItem.name: Closed error items
IntegrationErrorItem.countsFrom: From when the item was dismissed or retried (an open item is never due).

does.DELETE: Deletes the closed item (the failed message, its reason and tries); never an open one, never within 30 days of its close.
does.ANONYMISE: An error item cannot be anonymised: the rule only reports.
does.ARCHIVE: An error item cannot be archived: the rule only reports.

InboundEmail.name: Mails received
InboundEmail.countsFrom: From when the mail was received.

does.ANONYMISE: Blanks the sender, the envelope sender, the subject, the text and the HTML of a settled mail (matched, rejected or failed); the mail's place, time and status stay, and the record's thread keeps its own message.
does.DELETE: A received mail is never deleted by a sweep: the rule only reports.
does.ARCHIVE: A received mail cannot be archived by a sweep: the rule only reports.

ExportJob.name: Exports
ExportJob.countsFrom: From when the export was asked.

does.DELETE: The database never deletes an export (its file expires by itself): the rule only reports.
does.ANONYMISE: An export cannot be anonymised: the rule only reports.
does.ARCHIVE: An export cannot be archived: the rule only reports.

Invoice.name: Invoices
Invoice.countsFrom: From the issue date (a draft is never due).

does.ARCHIVE: Archives the issued invoice where it is: nothing is erased (the fiscal archive keeps the document and its file).
does.DELETE: An invoice is never deleted: the law keeps it 10 years.
does.ANONYMISE: An invoice is never anonymised: the law keeps it as issued.

other.name: Other records
other.countsFrom: The sweep knows nothing of this record type.
other.does: The sweep knows nothing of this record type: the rule only reports.

form.intro: One rule per record type and company; a company's own rule wins over the group's for its records.
form.groupOnly: These records belong to the whole group: one rule for every company.
form.reasonHint: The law that sets the period, for example c.c. art. 2220: 10 years.
form.asksCode: A shorter period (or another action while the rule applies) asks for a fresh code when you save.

held.group: These records belong to the whole group: pick Every company.
held.months: Keep it for whole months, from 1 to 1200.
held.noAction: No sweep may delete, anonymise or archive this record type: the rule can only report.
held.action: Pick what happens after the period.
held.reason: Say the legal reason (3 characters or more).
held.reasonLong: The legal reason is at most 1000 characters.

apply.title: Switch {type} ({company}) on to apply?
apply.from: From the next sweep, the records past the period are changed for real; a deleted record cannot be put back.
apply.unverified: The period is UNVERIFIED until the privacy consultant sets it.
apply.code: A fresh code from your authenticator is asked next.
apply.back: Back to reporting stops it at once.
apply.ack: I understand the sweep will change records for real.

done.added: Rule added for {type}: it only reports until switched on.
done.applyOn: {type}: the sweep now applies the rule.
done.sweptMany_one: 1 rule swept: a report, nothing changed.

ret.sweepSelectedNone: Only rules that are on and only report can be swept together; sweep an applying rule on its own.
ret.sweepSelectedLeft_one: 1 selected rule is left out (off, or it applies: sweep it on its own).
ret.sweepSelectedLeft_other: {count} selected rules are left out (off, or they apply: sweep them on their own).

ledgers.title: Kept for good, never purged
ledgers.intro: The database keeps these ledgers append-only: never swept, never offered for a rule.
ledgers.words: The Owner decided (15 November 2026): these ledgers are never purged after a period. An erasure request still blanks the person's details inside the change history; its rows stay.

AuditLog.name: Change history
AuditLog.what: Every change to a record, who made it and when.

ReadLog.name: Who looked
ReadLog.what: Who opened or downloaded a sensitive record.

SecurityEvent.name: Security events
SecurityEvent.what: Sign-ins, failed sign-ins, lockouts, role changes and exports.

StepUpAttempt.name: Fresh-code tries
StepUpAttempt.what: Every try of a fresh code.

purges.title: Purged on their own dates
purges.intro: These go by their own scheduled jobs, decided already; listed here so every way personal data leaves is in one place.

measurementPhotos.what: Body photos sent with measurements, made-to-measure office photos and fitting photos
measurementPhotos.when: 90 days after the garment ships (each on its own date); the measurements stay

portalCodes.why: GDPR art. 5(1)(e); kept a day for the security log

linkDrafts.what: Drafts of link forms (measurements, claims, questionnaires)

exportFiles.when: When the export expires (the export row stays)

accessPackages.what: A person's data package (the copy an access request collected)
accessPackages.when: 30 days after it was made (the request and its record of what was sent stay)
accessPackages.why: GDPR art. 5(1)(e): never kept as a second copy of the person's data

kept.title: Kept for good
kept.RetentionSweep: Every sweep and what it did

my.title: Download my data
my.intro: A copy of what the factory holds about you, in one ZIP (GDPR arts. 15 and 20):

holds.data: your data as data.json and one file per kind of record;
holds.readme: a README that explains each part, with the checksums.

my.asked: Asked: the copy is collected in the background and appears here when ready.

held.open: One request at a time: your last one is still open (download it first).
held.company: Pick the company you work in first (the switch at the top): the request is kept by that company.

my.none: You have not asked for your data yet.
my.handover: The first download hands the copy over: the request is then done. The link works for one minute.
